clue.text: Pirate, having met the Queen, could be prime minister once

indicators.note: the pirate joined by the Queen would make the former leader's surname, so taking the Queen away from that surname leaves the pirate

parts.note: Margaret Thatcher was UK prime minister from 1979 to 1990
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword Queen

explanation.surface: A buccaneer meets the monarch and might go on to lead the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackbeard, Edward Teach, was also known as Edward Thatch; add ER and you have the surname of a past prime minister. The clue works backwards from that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Thatch was an alternative name of Blackbeard, the notorious eighteenth-century buccaneer.

clue.text: Domestic pig gets up on tiptoe to dance

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the tiptoe letter above the rest

parts.note: the tip of toe is its first letter

indicators.note: gets up in a down clue means the domestic pig is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: a domestic animal is a pet
a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: A pet pig rises on its toes to dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiptoe' is read as the tip of 'toe', T.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-step is a ballroom dance in march or polka time.

clue.text: One-time insider, alias "Dog"

indicators.note: insider tells us one-time sits within the alias letters

parts.note: aka, also known as, means alias
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A former mole goes by the code name Dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Akita is a large Japanese breed of spitz dog.

clue.text: Cosy conga (line dancing?)

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A conga line makes a friendly, snug scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Congenial means pleasant and agreeable, the warm feel of a cosy setting.

clue.text: Vague promise that one may get paid

indicators.note: vague means unclear or loosely formed, so the letters of the next word are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A half-hearted pledge is offered to someone hoping for payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-time professional is a player who gets paid, though not as a full-time career.

clue.text: Recruit maid first to polish?

indicators.note: first says the maid comes before the recruit word

parts.note: a maid is female, she

indicators.note: to is read as a turning signal, the recruit word being written backwards up the down light

parts.note: to call up or call is to recruit

explanation.surface: Hire a maid first to do the polishing.
explanation.walkthrough: No word clearly signals the reversal; 'to' is the nearest candidate, read as turning the recruit word up the down light. The question mark flags polish as one use of the varnish.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin varnish used to give wood a glossy finish, as French polish.

clue.text: Out of military uniform, free to ignore their leaders

definitions.text: Out of military uniform, free to ignore their leaders

indicators.note: their leaders points to the first letter of each word in this run of the clue

explanation.surface: Off duty and out of uniform, soldiers are free to disregard their officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of' introduces the source of the letters, while the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mufti is civilian dress worn by someone who normally wears a uniform.

clue.text: You can read this statement of grievance from former time

parts.note: a plaint is a complaint or lament
ex means former

explanation.surface: A complaint from long ago that you can still read.
explanation.definitionFit: In cryptography, plain text is the unencrypted readable message.

clue.text: There might be gold here, in report of ball by journalist

indicators.note: by places the journalist next to the ball sound
report of means the word for ball is heard, sounding like a mineral plus a letter

parts.note: an orb is a ball or sphere
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Gold might lie here, in a journalist's account of a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: An ore bed is a layer of rock containing metal deposits, possibly gold.

clue.text: Dance round and round mid-ceilidh in Wick and surroundings

indicators.note: the second round means the shuffled letters go around the next piece
the first round means the letters of dance are turned about into a new order
mid points to the central letter of ceilidh

explanation.surface: Dancers whirl at a ceilidh in Wick, a town in the far north of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'round' rearranges DANCE into CANDE; the second puts it around L, the middle of 'ceilidh', a Scottish social dance. Wick is a Highland town, but here a wick.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle is a wick set in the wax that surrounds it.

clue.text: Fix position — which is north — and turn around, making a tiny adjustment

indicators.note: around tells us the shuffled turn letters go about the abbreviations for which is and north
a small change in arrangement signals that the letters of the turn word are shuffled

parts.note: to turn is to rotate
i.e. (id est) is Latin for which is, written IE
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A navigator fixes a position, notes north, and turns slightly to adjust course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a tiny adjustment' turns ROTATE into ORTATE, which goes 'around' IEN. 'Turn around' looks like one phrase but is split, and i.e. is Latin id est.
explanation.definitionFit: To orientate yourself is to work out where you are, establishing your bearings.

clue.text: Lover might lead sergeant in dance

indicators.note: the lover leading the sergeant gives the dance, so the dance with the sergeant removed from its end leaves the lover

parts.note: flamenco is a Spanish dance
a sergeant is an NCO, a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A romantic partner takes the lead in a dance with a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: The lover goes in front of the sergeant to make the Spanish dance, so the clue asks for whatever precedes the sergeant there.
explanation.definitionFit: An old flame is a former sweetheart, so a flame is a lover.

clue.text: Make fun of a type of dance the home counties follow

indicators.note: follow tells us the home counties come after the dance in the answer

parts.note: a tea dance is an afternoon dance with tea served
the home counties are the counties around London in South-East England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: Mocking the tea dances popular around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The home counties are the English counties surrounding London, in the south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: To tease someone is to mock or rib them playfully.

clue.text: Flirting with everyone during foxtrot, say

indicators.note: during means the everyone letters sit within the dance

parts.note: the foxtrot is an example of a dance, signalled by say
every gives ALL and one gives I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Flirting with all the partners on the floor during a foxtrot.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalliance is casual romantic play, trifling with someone's affections.

clue.text: American dance is last to demonstrate potential

parts.note: a prom is a formal US high-school dance

indicators.note: last to points to the final letter of demonstrate

explanation.surface: A US school dance is the final chance to show what someone can do.
explanation.definitionFit: Promise is a sign of future success, as in a youngster showing great potential.

clue.text: It's a mistake to show desire in public

indicators.note: in tells us the desire word sits inside the public word

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
to sigh for something is to show longing for it

explanation.surface: It is wrong to display longing openly.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is an error caused by failing to notice something.

clue.text: Stopped dance, as Eddie Cochran appeared

indicators.note: appeared says the answer shows up within the run of words that precedes it

explanation.surface: The dancing stopped, the way it did when Eddie Cochran turned up on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Eddie Cochran was a 1950s American rock and roll singer who died young, adding a sly second sense to 'Stopped'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceased is the past tense of cease, meaning came to an end or halted.

clue.text: Overflow from a bath tap?

parts.note: a Bath bun is a sweet bun from the city of Bath
tap is a kind of dance, the question mark marking an example

explanation.surface: Water spilling from a bath tap.
explanation.walkthrough: A Bath bun is a sugary bun from the English city of Bath; the capital is hidden at the start of the clue's lowercase 'bath'.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance is a plentiful supply, more than enough, a sense of overflowing.

clue.text: Dance homeland?

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A dance from one's native country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homeland' splits into 'home' (IN) and 'land', the definition; the question mark admits the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To land a fish an angler winds it towards the bank with the line.

clue.text: Houris from Asia end in disappointment

indicators.note: disappointment suggests things going wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Beautiful maidens from Asia end up a letdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Water nymphs of Greek myth, like the beautiful maidens of the Islamic paradise, are alluring female spirits.

clue.text: Fought in armour in judo and set in motion

indicators.note: in motion means moving about, so the letters of the two words are mixed

explanation.surface: Martial artists fight in judo and get things moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Knights jousted on horseback in armour, charging with lances.

clue.text: Dance was postponed? It's a puzzle

parts.note: a jig is a lively dance

indicators.note: postponed means put back, so the letters of was are turned round

explanation.surface: A dance was put off, which is a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigsaw is a picture cut into interlocking pieces to be reassembled.

clue.text: Without warning, calls "Don't be proud!"

parts.note: the phrase is read as an instruction to give up or abandon something
pride is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: Someone phones out of the blue to say not to be so haughty.
explanation.walkthrough: Pride is a deadly sin, so 'Don't be proud!' tells you to give up a sin.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay an unannounced visit is to call round unexpectedly.

clue.text: Spooner's dancing army is back

indicators.note: Spooner's means the opening sounds of the two words are swapped, after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: the rumba is a Cuban dance
a legion is a Roman army unit, or any large force

explanation.surface: A dancing army returns.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower part of the back, between ribs and pelvis, is the anatomical area behind the lower spine.

clue.text: Excited to be creating puzzles, if traumatic

parts.note: up means excited or keyed up
a crossword compiler is said to be setting puzzles

explanation.surface: A setter is thrilled to make puzzles, even if the solvers find them painful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something upsetting causes distress, as a traumatic event does.

clue.text: It's danced south of the Sierra

definitions.meaning: in the NATO alphabet the codeword for T comes after Sierra, for S, so in a down light it sits below

explanation.surface: A dance performed south of the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: Sierra is S in the radio alphabet, followed by T's codeword; 'south of' means below in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance that originated in Buenos Aires.

clue.text: Dance round and round

parts.note: a disc is a flat round object
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Dancers twirling round and round.
explanation.definitionFit: Disco is dancing to pop music in a club, popular in the 1970s.

clue.text: Fish, used creatively, fed characters going out

definitions.text: Fish, used creatively, fed characters going out

indicators.note: creatively means the letters of fish and used are reworked
characters going out says the letters of fed are removed from the mix

explanation.surface: Fish, used inventively, are fed to people as they go out.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix FISH USED, remove F, E and D, and five letters remain to be arranged; the whole clue describes the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is the Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish.

clue.text: Start endless dance? That's not acceptable

indicators.note: That's not tells us the letter for acceptable is removed
endless means the dance loses its final letter

parts.note: the beguine is a Caribbean ballroom dance
U means upper-class and so socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Someone launches an endless dance, which others find out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: U stands for upper-class, hence socially acceptable, a usage from Nancy Mitford's 'U and non-U'.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin is to commence or set something going.

clue.text: Wrongdoing, as is examiner's opinion

indicators.note: wrong means out of order, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A misdeed, judged as it stands, in an examiner's view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongdoing' is split: 'Wrong' is the anagram signal and 'doing' joins AS IS as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagnosis is a doctor's judgement of what illness a patient has after examination.

clue.text: Boatman backs Boatman on head of ship's victuals

indicators.note: backs means the first boatman word is turned round

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
Boatman is the setter, so he refers to himself as I

indicators.note: head of picks out the first letter of ship

explanation.surface: A boatman supports another boatman with the ship's food supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: Boatman is the setter's own pseudonym, so the second one is I.
explanation.definitionFit: Rations are fixed allowances of food, the provisions issued aboard ship.

clue.text: See 21
